reviews.title: The UI is an Afterthought
reviews.text:
Multiple UI elements in the editor cover each other. When trying to select something it will almost never select the correct thing if there is even the slightest overlap. Theres no way to select something underneath another element without manually sending the entire layer “to the back” so you can select what it was on top of.

One of the most egregious things Canva does is wholly ignore all edits made to a photo from your phone. If you use your photos app to edit something, especially using markdown to add shapes/other elements, Canva will elect to ignore them on import. The imported image will be automatically reverted to its unedited original with no way to change it back.

Theres just so many small issues with the UI it’s unbelievable. Actively hinders production and makes the entire process endlessly frustrating. Most of the “skill” in using Canva is just learning how to navigate the myriad of terribly designed UI elements.

It also encourages the use of AI slop. The app is literally trying to make you dependent on its slop generator. It wants you to lose your actual graphic design skills. Everything you make also gets automatically stolen and fed into their plagiarism machine.

reviews.title: Artificial (Not) Intelligence
reviews.text:
It is incredibly frustrating to watch an AI burn app through your limited teat credits on the exact same mistakes without ever learning from its previous attempts. Limiting users testing the product by the number of prompt attempts instead of successful completed images completely penalizes you for the AI's own mistakes. It is a terrible user experience and a terrible way to convince someone to upgrade.
Canva's image generator relies on a lighter, fast-processing AI engine that struggles heavily with complex scenes that contain more than three or four specific details.
If you want an AI image generator that actually follows complex, multi-object instructions without immediately locking you out or forcing an upgrade, there are better alternatives until they improve their AI and usage model.

I was just now fighting with a glitchy laggy reactions with the ipad app, and a popup appeared asking me to rate and review this service. Sometimes it is hidden below the screen.  Other times it is on the top of the interface somewhere.  Other times it is missing altogether.  This platform is a total mess. reviews.title: AI is Extreme, Wish There Was an AI Free Version
reviews.text:
I loved Canva when it first came out and used it extensively for years for my NGO in particular but also for other part-time jobs and consulting projects. But ever since it went from dipping its toes in AI to full on AI worshipper it has gone completely downhill and I try to avoid using it at all. I know technically you are supposed to be able to still use it without the AI features, but they have built them in so deeply they have made it impossible to get anything done without using AI. And I also know ethically and environmentally I’m not really making a difference if I still use an app this heavy into AI even if I avoid some obvious usage of AI, it is still underneath it all. Canva was perfectly great without AI, you guys are capable of designing an app that allows the average person to - I wont’t say graphic design because that is an actual profession with way more skills-but to make cohesively designed branding and presentation documents and some light video and photo
editing without the HUGE moral implications & rushing the planet towards destruction, just so startups can add a tiny animated video of a monkey to their newsletter!

reviews.title: Buggy and Confusing
reviews.text: I’ve been using canva pro for work and it has been an uphill climb. I have clips on my phone, which I’ll try to edit on my computer by uploading to canva, which little did I know is actually a trap. Clip uploading starts by teasing you by showing you your entire clip, then turns your screen into a gradient white/grey loading screen. You literally can’t do anything but stare at it and it doesn’t even work. Waited for half an hour, gave up, came back 2 days later and it says the clip couldn’t be uploaded. So now I’m forced to do everything on my tiny phone screen which canva clearly wasn’t built for. Because now I’m trying to edit a clip by adding “elements”, which is another buggy issue because it ends up taking a horizontal tag I (somehow successfully) uploaded and blows up a small portion of it to take up the whole vertical project. Doesn’t even let me shrink it down or resize it either, just takes a general idea and doesn’t let me look at anything other than canva’s interpretation of what it should look like because it’s now taking up literally the whole project’s screen. It ends up taking about 20 minutes just to process a 1 minute video. I think I’ll try CapCut.

reviews.title: BUYER BEWARE!!!
reviews.text: I have been using Canva Pro and the free version since 2021. Mostly for stock photos and video footage to use as fillers on social media. I’ve never had any major issues with the company till now. I recently changed my niche. Now I need Ai generated images and video clips. Because of the years of trust I had for this company I don’t hesitate to buy a Canva Pro plan for another year. They were selling their AI model as superior and I believed it. Right after I make my payment to Apple I generated my first image. I could not believe how bad it was. I gave AI simple and direct instructions it still could not follow. The majority of the images I attempted to make came out distorted, backwards or some other odd and unnatural look. I tried multiple times to contact customer service, it’s not even possible. There is no human support anymore, only AI automated. I contacted Apple to get a refund, it was denied twice with no explanation. Even though Canva is selling a faulty AI product. I was also forewarned not to push refunds with Apple because they will strip you of access to all of your Google accounts including your email! Apple gets 30% of every subscription we buy. No wonder they want to keep your money. This has become a digital mafia. I will never again buy anything from Canva. Be careful what you buy that’s connected with Apple!!!

reviews.title: Unremivable danger zone warning
reviews.text:
I used to love Canva, I pay full subscription, but without asking they’ve added “Danger zone” warning red boxes around all my designs. There is no way to remove them.

They block my view of what is behind them and impede my ability to properly design my image in the frame I have chosen to use. If I wanted a smaller frame I’d choose one. Why is there no way to get rid of the warnings???

They are for printing but (1) I never print the majority of my designs (2) If I am printing I want to design over the bleed zone, that is the whole point of it, so 
I can’t see what is there and if it is printed it still looks good.

This forced red boxes stops me from seeing what is under it properly and tricks my eye when assessing the overall design. I AM NOT PRINTING. A very very large number of users fall into the same category. Why are you forcing us to not be able to properly see or design our images? I m not printing!

This has ruined it for me, I want my money back.
